title: Public health burnout, political interference, and retention
discussion_signal: The post circulates public-health worker burnout and political-interference findings, then reflects on the emotional and professional difficulty of responding to hostile public discussion. It connects institutional strain to retention risk and the meaning of public service work.
linked_research_question: How do strain, political interference, and public hostility alter public-health workers' willingness and ability to remain in the institution?
limits: The post is a personal interpretation of survey results
Self-selected professional discussion is not a representative worker sample
Reported strain does not identify which retention intervention will work
